mission: We think every lab bench should be able to run PCR. So we're building a PCR machine out of air.

people.name: Baris Özdinç
people.creds: PhD candidate in Microbiology, Wageningen University & Research
people.plain: Uses PCR every day in his research, studying gut bacteria in hundreds of samples. He knows what you need from a PCR machine.

people.name: Pavlo Hrab, PhD
people.plain: Writes software and analyses data to understand biology. At AirPCR he leads the simulation, the open-source software and the AI integration.

principles.title: Model first, then build.
principles.text: We test ideas in a computer before we cut a single part.

principles.title: Measure everything.
principles.text: Every claim gets checked on the bench, and we say which numbers are measured.

principles.title: Open by default.
principles.text: Open data, open connections, parts anyone can buy.
